stories.title: URA expands GFA exemptions, BCA enhances funding support for green building retrofits - The Edge Singapore
Canary Wharf student housing claims world record
stories.summary: Urbanest Canary Wharf has been certified as the world's tallest Passivhaus building. The 46-storey cluster provides 1,672 beds for UCL students, alongside a gym, yoga studio, cinema rooms, and a McDonald’s drive-thru. The building is officially designed to be as efficient as possible while serving fast food.

stories.title: ACE Powerhouse wins second sustainability award
stories.summary: ACE Powerhouse at Campus Skellefteå has received the MB Plus Project of the Year award at the 2026 Sweden Green Building Awards. This follows its recognition as Environmental Building of the Year in 2025. The project is described as a testament to long-term sustainability and innovative collaboration.

stories.title: Passivhaus Institute certifies 136.8-metre London tower
stories.summary: The Passivhaus Institute has certified the 46-storey urbanest Canary Wharf complex as the world's tallest and largest residential Passivhaus building. The project houses 1,672 students across three towers. The developer announced the certification on November 25, confirming the site meets the institute's requirements for energy efficiency.

stories.title: DS Group's Renaissance Bengaluru Race Course Hotel Achieves LEED Platinum Certification - India Education Diary
CII IGBC and University of Mumbai sign MoU to strengthen green education and develop industry-ready talent for sustainab
IGBC and University of Mumbai partner for green education
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council and the University of Mumbai have signed a memorandum of understanding to develop a specialised course on the green built environment. The partnership aims to train engineering students in sustainable practices, following an agreement signed at the Green Education Conclave 2026.

stories.title: Stanbic Bank Kenya secures dual green certifications
stories.summary: Stanbic Bank Kenya has received EDGE Advanced and Net Zero Carbon certifications for its refurbished headquarters in Westlands. The bank stated the project demonstrates that sustainability excellence is achievable through the responsible transformation of existing structures. The building is now officially future-ready and environmentally responsible.

stories.title: Student digs in Canary Wharf named 'world's tallest' Passivhaus building - BusinessGreen
Kochi home designed to follow natural terrain
stories.summary: The House of Stepped Gardens in Kochi is designed to mirror the contours of its site rather than flattening the land. The architecture unfolds through cascading split levels intended to respond to the earth's profile. The project covers 3,200 square feet and relies on the landscape for its structure.

stories.title: Kerakoll India Marks Two Decades of Innovation, Growth and Sustainable Building in India - Press Trust of India
Phoenix Mills begins transformation of Kurla office district
stories.summary: The Phoenix Mills is upgrading its 23-acre office district in Kurla, including Art Guild House and Phoenix Paragon. The programme aims to enhance architectural expression and shared landscapes to improve the experience for modern occupiers. The developer notes that workplace value extends beyond the buildings themselves.

stories.title: Restoration stalled at Lucknow's Rifa-e-Aam Club
stories.summary: Restoration work at the historic Rifa-e-Aam Club in Lucknow has been stalled for four months. The site, once a hub for writers and political leaders, currently features waterlogged grounds and construction materials. Security guards at the premises report that the reasons for the delay remain unknown.

stories.title: Take a tour inside 18000 sq ft TruNativ’s Mumbai office that reimagines the language of corporate interiors - Architect
Take a tour inside the 2500 sq ft Mumbai residence that finds its character in simplicity - Architect and Interiors Indi
From a demolished Delhi home to Ladakhi architecture: Inside India’s Venice Biennale win - شبكة تواصل الإخبارية
Ladakh ancestral home converted into artist residency
stories.summary: A 250-year-old, five-storey house in Nimmu has been repurposed as an artist residency. Previously owned by the Rupchan family for seven generations, the building is located on a hill slope 35 kilometres from Leh. It was featured as part of the inaugural Sā Biennale this year.

stories.title: Take a look inside the 2300 sq ft Yapral residence that is rooted in people-first approach - Architect and Interiors Ind
Sinuous stone-roofed visitor center meanders through the mountains of China
stories.summary: The Huangguoshu Scenic Area in China features two visitor centers designed by the China Academy of Urban Planning and Design and AEPA&TSC. The architects say the sweeping, serpentine roofs take their formal cues from the movement of the local Baishui River. The water is currently stationary.

stories.title: O’Donnell + Tuomey wins 2026 Building Beauty Awards
stories.summary: The Dublin-based firm O’Donnell + Tuomey has been named the winner of this year’s Building Beauty Awards. The practice was established by Sheila O’Donnell and John Tuomey, who are both professors emeriti at the UCD School of Architecture, Planning & Environmental Policy. The award recognizes their work on university buildings.

stories.title: Rolex building by David Chipperfield nears grand completion
stories.summary: The new 30-story Rolex headquarters on Fifth Avenue is nearing completion. Designed by David Chipperfield Architects, the 143-meter glass tower replaces a 12-story structure that had occupied the site since the 1970s. The building is now turning on its lights to signal its presence to the skyline.

stories.title: Europe's largest museum development opens in Citroën garage
stories.summary: The former Citroën Garage in Brussels has been converted into Kanal, a 40,000-square-metre museum for modern art and architecture. The project, designed by a consortium of three architecture studios, claims to be Europe’s largest museum development. It includes three new volumes added to the original 1930s industrial structure.

stories.title: RSHP centres cantilevered office building Sąvaržėlė around glass atrium
stories.summary: UK studio RSHP has completed Sąvaržėlė, a seven-storey office building in Vilnius, Lithuania. The firm describes the cantilevered, stacked structure as a landmark that is unmistakably forward-looking. The building is named after the Lithuanian word for paperclip and houses office space, a conference hall, and a restaurant.

stories.title: Carlo Ratti and AI assistant to curate Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism 2027
stories.summary: Architect Carlo Ratti will curate the 2027 Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism using an unconventional, AI-based approach. Ratti intends to use the event to question the current role of a curator. The full curatorial team and the theme remain undisclosed until December 8.

stories.title: Thermally modified wood awards: reed-roofed guesthouses
stories.summary: Four projects were named winners of the 2026 Thermory Design Awards, which recognize structures built with thermally modified wood. The competition received 78 entries from 23 countries. The awards are sponsored by Thermory, and the jury includes representatives from the company.

stories.title: Clustered cycladic village residences shape Aristides Dallas Architects’ hospitality masterplan
stories.summary: Aristides Dallas Architects has designed Shared Ground, a hospitality masterplan on a Greek island. The studio says the project explores how architecture can bring together privacy and community by staggering low-rise volumes along the natural contours of a hillside. The buildings are angled away from the sea.

stories.title: Bukhara Biennial 2027 announces theme and first artists
stories.summary: The Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation has announced The Long Welcome as the theme for the second Bukhara Biennial, running from September to November 2027. Led by artistic director Kulapat Yantrasast, the event aims to leave a lasting legacy through new commissions created exclusively within the country.

stories.title: Heidelberg Materials supplies in-situ carbon negative concrete
stories.summary: Heidelberg Materials UK has partnered with BAM UK and Ireland and the Environment Agency to deliver the UK's first carbon-negative in-situ concrete. The project incorporates ACLA technology to achieve its carbon-negative status. The companies collaborated to complete the installation.

stories.title: FPA wins London Construction Award for mass timber research
stories.summary: The Fire Protection Association has won a 2026 London Construction Award for research into sprinkler protection for mass timber buildings. The project developed a design methodology for buildings with exposed cross laminated timber surfaces. The research was conducted over a three-year period ending in December 2025.

stories.title: Green steel market projected to grow to USD 29.72 billion by 2036
stories.summary: Future Market Insights estimates the global green steel market will reach USD 4.80 billion in 2026. The report projects a compound annual growth rate of 20 percent over the next decade. Industry development is attributed to decarbonization targets and hydrogen-based ironmaking technologies.

stories.title: Architectural metalwork market enters 2026 with new procurement trends
stories.summary: The global architectural metalwork market is entering a period defined by decarbonization mandates and the industrialization of construction, according to IndexBox. The sector is seeing more disciplined procurement behavior and a regionally diversified supply architecture. The market covers everything from structural framing to decorative metal elements.

stories.title: Random forest model predicts construction cost deviations
stories.summary: A research team has introduced an AI-driven framework to forecast budget overruns and schedule delays in construction projects. Published in the journal Discover Artificial Intelligence, the model uses machine learning to analyze static blueprints. The authors claim the system identifies logistical bottlenecks that conventional monitoring tools often miss.

stories.title: 3D printing in construction market projected for high growth
stories.summary: DataM Intelligence reports the global 3D printing in construction market was valued at USD 8.28 billion in 2025. The firm projects the market will reach USD 6,431.95 billion by 2035, representing a compound annual growth rate of 94.55 percent. The growth is attributed to automated building technologies.

stories.title: Autodesk and Neilsoft join forces to set up AECO Centre of Excellence in Pune
stories.summary: Autodesk and Neilsoft are establishing a Centre of Excellence in Pune to promote BIM, digital twins, and AI-powered technologies. The partnership combines Autodesk's cloud platform with Neilsoft's engineering expertise. The initiative aims to support digital transformation across the built environment lifecycle in India and global markets.

stories.title: Allplan Max introduces AI capabilities for engineering workflows
stories.summary: Allplan has launched Allplan Max, a suite of AI-powered tools for its 2027 software release. The company says the features are designed to automate routine tasks and help engineers navigate complex models. The stated goal is to keep engineering judgment firmly in the hands of the professionals.

stories.title: JA ESS names GIL Automations as authorised service partner
stories.summary: GIL Automations has been certified as the authorized service partner for JA Battery Energy Storage Systems in Africa. The partnership covers technical support and maintenance for the company's energy storage products. The firms aim to accelerate the adoption of resilient energy solutions across the continent.

stories.title: Bangladesh looks to architecture for climate resilience
stories.summary: The 2026 UN Climate Change Conference has prompted calls for Bangladesh to rethink its construction industry and integrate climate-responsive design into national development. The country faces rising sea levels, heatwaves, and floods that are already reshaping its built environment and the daily lives of its population.

stories.title: Cool roof tiles are not a magic fix for Indian summers
stories.summary: Industry experts suggest that marketing claims regarding cool roof tiles often overstate their ability to lower indoor temperatures or halve electricity bills. While the tiles can assist in cooling homes, they are not a replacement for comprehensive passive cooling or effective building design in hot climates.

stories.title: Lepcha engineering remains a lifeline in North Sikkim
stories.summary: Following the 2023 glacial lake outburst flood, infrastructure across North Sikkim was severed, isolating regions like Dzongu. As local distrust in state systems grows, the resilience of traditional engineering and routes remains a point of focus for communities waiting for long-term road restoration efforts to conclude.

stories.title: Sacred groves preserve biodiversity through centuries of faith
stories.summary: Communities across India continue to protect forest pockets known as sacred groves, including Maharashtra's Devrais and Rajasthan's Orans. These areas remain untouched by development or timber harvesting, preserved instead by long-standing traditions that maintain a specific relationship between local populations and their surrounding natural landscapes.

stories.title: Do Roof Tiles Reduce Indoor Heat? India Is Finding Out. - The New York Times
Hostile architecture targets wildlife in urban India
stories.summary: Planners are increasingly using hostile architecture to deter animals from entering public spaces. This design approach, which also includes anti-homeless measures, renders structures intentionally unusable for specific groups. As urban areas expand, green spaces are being replaced by designs that prioritize exclusion over shared utility.

stories.title: CEPT students develop smart leak detection system
stories.summary: Seven students at CEPT University have created HydroSense, a system designed to pinpoint concealed pipeline leaks within 5 cm. The technology aims to prevent the damp walls and costly repairs associated with undetected plumbing failures. The system can also automatically shut off water supplies when leaks occur.

stories.title: Gurugram to repurpose parks for flood management
stories.summary: After spending hundreds of crores on drains that failed to prevent monsoon flooding, Haryana officials will now convert 247 acres of city parks into retention ponds. The plan includes installing rainwater harvesting structures to recharge groundwater, marking a departure from the previous reliance on traditional drainage systems.

stories.title: Hyderabad faces urban strain amid rapid expansion
stories.summary: Hyderabad is experiencing significant infrastructure pressure, including chronic traffic gridlocks and depleting groundwater. Despite its status as a global tech hub, the city's drainage networks and public amenities are struggling to keep pace with the scale of recent construction and rapid urban development.

stories.title: Telangana CM pushes for Musi River rejuvenation
stories.summary: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy has ordered officials to expedite urban development projects, including the Musi River Rejuvenation and radial road construction. Phase-1 of the river project involves designating specific stretches of the waterway for development, following a review of the state's municipal and urban infrastructure plans.

stories.title: Defining the inclusive city in an era of inequality
stories.summary: Urban policy is increasingly focused on the inclusive city, aiming to ensure public spaces remain accessible despite widening inequality and aging populations. Experts argue that true inclusivity requires creating conditions where diverse groups can coexist, rather than simply providing basic physical access to urban environments.

stories.title: Government hosts workshop on urban infrastructure financing
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs held a workshop on 26 November to help cities secure market-based financing for infrastructure projects. Municipal commissioners from 25 cities attended to discuss bankable project development with representatives from the Asian Development Bank and other financial institutions.

stories.title: Karnataka cities face pressure from rapid urban growth
stories.summary: As Karnataka's urban centers expand, local administrations are struggling to manage rising water demand, waste, and traffic. While Bengaluru remains the most prominent example, smaller cities like Mysuru and Hubballi-Dharwad are also facing the challenge of scaling their municipal systems to match their rapid population growth.

stories.title: Karnataka cities prepare for climate-related infrastructure risks
stories.summary: Karnataka is evaluating its urban planning to address climate risks, including heavy rainfall and rising temperatures. Officials note that these environmental shifts are no longer future concerns but are currently impacting public health and infrastructure, requiring a change in how the state's cities operate and expand.

stories.title: Asia and Africa to lead global urban growth
stories.summary: Cities are expected to accommodate two-thirds of global population growth by 2050. While Africa's urban population is projected to double, Asia currently hosts 19 of the world's 33 megacities. Many small and medium-sized cities in these regions are also experiencing rapid growth, centralizing their role in global transformation.

stories.title: Toyota and JSW Steel sign separate infrastructure MoUs
stories.summary: Toyota Kirloskar Motor has signed a road safety agreement with Varanasi Smart City. Separately, JSW Steel and JAKSON Green have partnered with MCi Carbon to evaluate technology that converts steel slag and CO2 into carbon-embedded materials, aiming to test the commercial feasibility of mineral carbonation in India.

stories.title: MCD issues new inspection rules for heritage buildings
stories.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has established a standard operating procedure for the inspection and repair of 1,318 heritage structures. The move follows Supreme Court criticism regarding previous assessment discrepancies, and the new protocol applies to both government-owned and private properties within the city's jurisdiction.

stories.title: Punjab begins construction on 519 km of surface drains
stories.summary: The Punjab government has launched a project to construct 519 kilometres of surface drains across 49 cities. The initiative includes the rapid development of 45 disposal stations, with plans to rehabilitate 85 additional stations, as part of the ongoing Punjab Development Programme.

stories.title: Pulley raises $41M Series B to speed up construction permitting - Dealroom
PRISM BI adds conversational analytics to Microsoft Fabric
stories.summary: PRISM BI has launched an analytics application designed to connect with Microsoft Fabric. The tool features a semantic layer, an AI engine for query generation, and a React-based visualisation interface. It supports 14 chart types and allows users to customise colours and interact with data through cross-filtering.

stories.title: Kilo ranks itself top of digital twin platforms
stories.summary: Kilo has released a ranking of digital twin platforms for 2026. The list places Kilo’s own digital building twin at the top, ahead of six established enterprise competitors. The company claims its platform is best suited for handling multi-protocol sensor data across smart buildings and industrial facilities.

stories.title: AI construction tools find changes but not solutions
stories.summary: AI tools are increasingly used in construction to compare drawings and flag discrepancies, such as a moved manhole. While the software identifies changes, the site team must still determine if the adjustment is suitable for the work. Finding the problem is not the same as finishing the job.

stories.title: PCO raises $1.3 million for AI video optimization
stories.summary: Busan-based PCO has raised $1.3 million in a pre-Series A round and secured selection for the 2026 Scale-up TIPS program. The company, which develops AI-based video transmission technology, is eligible for an additional $1.5 million in government R&D funding. Its total growth capital now stands at $2.8 million.

stories.title: India data centre funding surges 11-fold
stories.summary: Disclosed funding for India’s data centre infrastructure reached ₹16,458.52 crore in 2026, an 11-fold increase over the previous year. Four operators cornered 99.9 per cent of the total inflows, leaving minimal capital for early-stage startups. Equity deals accounted for 92 per cent of the year's total funding.

stories.title: BirlaNu creates digital platform for architects
stories.summary: Building materials maker BirlaNu Limited has incorporated a subsidiary, MaterialFolio Innovations, to operate a digital platform for architects and interior designers. The move shifts the company beyond its core business of pipes and construction chemicals into a technology venture serving the professionals who specify its products.

stories.title: Japan's DataLabs raises capital from Yachiyo Engineering, Great Wave Ventures - Dealroom
GAIL plans entry into data centre market
stories.summary: State-owned gas transporter GAIL plans to enter the data centre industry with a 5 MW facility in Faridabad. The company intends to leverage its existing optical fibre network and land banks for the project. It is currently seeking an established operator for an equal joint venture.

stories.title: Royal Society for Arts names 2026 designers
stories.summary: The Royal Society for Arts has announced its 2026 cohort of Royal Designers for Industry. The six recipients include professionals from fields ranging from landscape architecture to costume design. The title is restricted to 200 designers at any one time, a limit maintained since the awards began in 1936.

stories.title: Royal Society for Arts adds five designers
stories.summary: The Royal Society for Arts has appointed five new Royal Designers for Industry and one honorary member. The awards recognise talent across architecture, technology, and the arts. The programme, which celebrates its 90th anniversary this year, limits the total number of active holders to 200 designers.

stories.title: KTH architecture school considers studio space cuts
stories.summary: The ABE School is evaluating a proposal to reduce architecture studio floor space by one-third from autumn 2027. The school cites structural financial challenges, noting that revenue from educational programmes no longer covers the costs of current premises. Rental costs rose sharply between 2021 and 2026.

stories.title: SRM University B.Arch admission 2027
stories.summary: College Mentor is providing information on eligibility criteria and application processes for the 2027 B.Arch programme at SRM University. The platform connects prospective students with mentors to share experiences and educational insights.

stories.title: CEPT University president on industry-oriented education
stories.summary: Prof Barjor Mehta of CEPT University discussed the need for higher education to bridge the gap between academic learning and professional practice. He emphasised the role of studio-based teaching and the integration of AI in preparing students to address housing and infrastructure challenges in Indian cities.

stories.title: Design educator questions student powerlessness
stories.summary: Céline Semaan writes that design education must evolve to address the political and ecological systems behind production. Reflecting on her time teaching at the School of Visual Arts, she noted that students often feel convinced of their own powerlessness in the face of planetary collapse.

stories.title: Architect reflects on the value of rough sketches
stories.summary: Architect Fergus Connolly reflects on the importance of sketching as a tool for communication and thought. Drawing from the work of historical architects like Hawksmoor and Soane, he argues that instinctive and incomplete drawings remain essential for the design process.

research.summary: More than a mile beneath the surface of the Red Sea, scientists have discovered rare underwater lakes that could reveal secrets about Earth's ancient oceans and the possibility of alien life.
